entities.name: PMID:25449986
observations: In irradiated male LDLR−/− mice reconstituted with blotchy or control marrow and infused with angiotensin II at 1,000 ng/kg/min for 4 weeks, blotchy marrow did not significantly alter plasma or hematopoietic-cell copper concentrations.
Angiotensin II increased thoracic and abdominal aortic diameters, but marrow groups did not differ significantly; rupture incidence was also not significantly different (P=0.10).
Blotchy-marrow recipients had significantly lower plasma MIP-1β, MCP-1, MCP-3, MCP-5, TIMP-1, and VEGF-A than control-marrow recipients (P<0.05).

entities.name: Atp7a
observations: The blotchy mouse phenotype involves an Atp7a mutation associated with copper deficiency; this is the donor-marrow genotype in PMID:25449986.

entities.name: LDLR deficiency
observations: LDLR−/− mice were the irradiated recipients in the chronic angiotensin II bone-marrow reconstitution model.

entities.name: Blotchy marrow copper effect
observations: In LDLR−/− recipients during 4 weeks of angiotensin II infusion, blotchy versus control marrow produced no significant difference in plasma or hematopoietic-cell copper concentrations.

entities.name: Blotchy marrow aortic effect
observations: In LDLR−/− recipients during angiotensin II infusion, blotchy versus control marrow produced no significant difference in aortic diameters or rupture incidence; rupture incidence P=0.10.

entities.name: Blotchy marrow mediators
observations: Blotchy marrow was associated with significantly lower circulating MIP-1β, MCP-1, MCP-3, MCP-5, TIMP-1, and VEGF-A than control marrow (P<0.05), indicating a marrow-dependent inflammatory mediator effect.
